name: How does the 'identification rule' work for replacement properties in a South Florida 1031 Exchange?

mainEntity.name: How does the 'identification rule' work for replacement properties in a South Florida 1031 Exchange?

acceptedAnswer.text: The identification rule requires you to formally identify potential replacement properties within 45 calendar days of closing on your relinquished property. You must deliver a written, unambiguous identification to your qualified intermediary. There are typically three rules for identification: the 'Three Property Rule' (identify up to three properties regardless of value), the '200% Rule' (identify any number of properties as long as their aggregate fair market value does not exceed 200% of the relinquished property's value), or the '95% Rule' (acquire at least 95% of the fair market value of all properties identified, regardless of number). We can assist in sourcing potential properties across our service areas that fit these criteria.
acceptedAnswer.description: Within 45 days of selling your property, you must formally identify replacement properties to your qualified intermediary using one of three IRS rules: the Three Property Rule, the 200% Rule, or the 95% Rule. This identification must be written and unambiguous.
